# Test fixtures

Three unrelated things live here. The `GeneralStateTests/` tree is vendored from
`ethereum/tests`; the `console-log/` tree is vendored from Hardhat and forge-std;
`dumpstate-flat-layout.json` is one of ours.

## `dumpstate-flat-layout.json` — a `dumpState()` captured from the PRE-OVERLAY build

Captured 2026-08-09 from the node as it shipped BEFORE
[ADR 0009](../../../../docs/adr/0009-none-mode-storage-is-per-account-with-per-checkpoint-overlays.md)
re-layered the node's storage, i.e. while storage was still
`SimpleStateManager`'s one flat `${address}_${slot}` map.

It exists because `dumpState` output is **persisted data** (IndexedDB, `loadState`
fixtures) with existing state behind it, so the internal layout is free to move
under it and the serialised format is not. `../storage-overlay.spec.ts` uses it
twice: it rebuilds the identical state on the current code and asserts the
`accounts`/`code`/`storage` sections are **byte-identical** (key ORDER included),
and it `loadState`s this very file into a fresh node and reads the values back.

The state it holds is mixed on purpose: pre-state storage, storage written by the
EVM through nested checkpoints, a CREATE (which calls `clearStorage`) that also
writes a slot, a cheat giving storage to an account that had none, and a cheat
appending a slot to an account that had some — so it exercises grouping AND
within-account ordering. `blocks` carries a wall-clock genesis timestamp, so it is
not byte-compared; only the three state sections are.

It is also the proof that an OLD dump still loads after `computeStateRoot` replaced the `'none' | 'trie'` mode option (2026-09-28): it carries the informational top-level mode field (`"none"`) that nodes wrote before then. A node no longer writes it and ignores it on load, and `../storage-overlay.spec.ts` asserts both (the load, and that this is the one top-level field a fresh dump lacks).

**Do not regenerate it.** Its whole value is that it came from the older code; a
fresh capture from the current build would assert nothing.

**Provenance CHECKED, not merely attested (2026-08-09).** Because that last
sentence is the entire load-bearing claim, and a fixture generated by the new
code would make the byte-identity assertion pass vacuously, it was verified
independently: the scenario in `../helpers/storage-overlay.ts` was replayed
against a build of commit `088a30f`, the last commit BEFORE the re-layer, and the
resulting `accounts` / `code` / `storage` sections matched this file exactly,
key order included. So the assertion is comparing the current code against a
genuinely older capture. If you ever need to re-verify, do the same thing: build
that commit, replay `buildFixtureNode`'s scenario, diff the three sections.

## Vendored `ethereum/tests` fixtures (for track B conformance)

These are a **small, hand-picked handful** of canonical Ethereum
`GeneralStateTests` JSON files, copied verbatim, used by
[`../statetest.spec.ts`](../statetest.spec.ts) to conformance-test the node's
opt-in `computeStateRoot: true` against real spec fixtures (assert the post-state
Merkle-Patricia root + `keccak(RLP(logs))` match the fixture's expected values).

We vendor **only these files** (not the multi-hundred-MB repo).

## Source

- Repository: <https://github.com/ethereum/tests>
- **Tag: `v17.0`** (pinned; record this if you re-pull)
- Path in repo: `GeneralStateTests/stExample/`
- Pulled: 2026-06-02

## Files

| file | what it exercises |
|---|---|
| `GeneralStateTests/stExample/add11.json` | minimal: a legacy tx calling a tiny `(add 1 1) → SSTORE` contract (1 storage write, no logs) |
| `GeneralStateTests/stExample/eip1559.json` | an EIP-1559 (type-2) transaction |
| `GeneralStateTests/stExample/accessListExample.json` | an EIP-2930/1559 access-list transaction (2 data-index cases) |
| `GeneralStateTests/stExample/solidityExample.json` | a Solidity-compiled contract call |

## Format notes (why this works against the trie-less-by-default node)

Each fixture has a `pre` (genesis accounts), a `transaction`, an `env` (block
environment), and `post.<Fork>[]` cases. Each modern Cancun case carries a
**`txbytes`** field = the exact signed raw tx for that `{data,gas,value}` index
permutation, plus the expected post-state `hash` (the MPT state root) and `logs`
(`keccak(RLP(logs))`). The runner loads `pre` via the node's `initialState`
option, applies `env` via `blockEnv`, submits `txbytes` through
`eth_sendRawTransaction`, then compares `node.getStateRoot()` to `hash`. This only
works with `computeStateRoot: true` (the default computes no root, by design), which is
exactly the point of that opt-in.

## Vendored Solidity console libraries (for `webevm/console-log`)

The three libraries whose calls `webevm/console-log` decodes, copied verbatim with their licences, used by [`../console-log.spec.ts`](../console-log.spec.ts): it parses every function signature out of them and asserts that the selector table in `src/console-log-decoder.ts` is exactly those signatures plus their legacy `uint` / `int` aliases (minus forge-std's array-taking `console.table`, a decision recorded in that file), and that each one decodes. Pulled 2026-11-24, each at its repository's latest release tag on that day.

| file | repository | tag | commit | path in repo | licence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `console-log/hardhat/console.sol` | <https://github.com/NomicFoundation/hardhat> | `hardhat@3.22.0` | `0edb1e0f26ba2d0805785b7e868bfe6da5989da4` | `packages/hardhat/console.sol` | MIT, `console-log/hardhat/LICENSE` (from `packages/hardhat/LICENSE`) |
| `console-log/forge-std/console.sol` | <https://github.com/foundry-rs/forge-std> | `v1.17.0` | `f3dae6e6ee381f25eb6a246f7da9b85c91a68219` | `src/console.sol` | MIT OR Apache-2.0, `console-log/forge-std/LICENSE-MIT` and `LICENSE-APACHE` |
| `console-log/forge-std/console2.sol` | <https://github.com/foundry-rs/forge-std> | `v1.17.0` | `f3dae6e6ee381f25eb6a246f7da9b85c91a68219` | `src/console2.sol` | as above |

At this pin forge-std's `console2.sol` is a one-line re-export of `console.sol` (`import {console as console2} from "./console.sol";`), so it adds no signature of its own; the spec asserts that, so a re-pin where it diverges again is noticed. forge-std's `console.sol` has one `log` overload Hardhat's lacks, `log(string,int256)`, and twelve `table(...)` functions taking arrays.

To re-pull, fetch the same paths at the new tags (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<repo>/<tag>/<path>`), update this table, and run the spec: a signature the generated table does not produce, or one it produces that the files do not declare, fails it.
